- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3–4% above prior peak.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-period, model lags in adjusting; anticipate upward correction 1–2 days ahead.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show price moving away from 75–80 range, model tends to overreact; dampen forecast toward historical mean.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overpredicts late-period (last 7–10 days) if sentiment is bullish; reduce final 5–7 days’ forecast by 1–2%.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.67” or “0.33” alternation, model exhibits oscillation bias — smooth transitions, avoid abrupt swings.
